newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CRICKET-BORDER DOUBTS WEST INDIES WILL WIN A TEST.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-BORDER DOUBTS WEST INDIES WILL WIN A TEST.

text.p: Former Australia captain Allan Border on Wednesday said he doubted West Indies would win a test this southern summer, describing the former undisputed world champions of cricket as "downtrodden" after a second test loss.

In a column in Sydney's Daily Telegraph newspaper, Border wrote that West Indies would not be competitive unless key players such as star batsman Brian Lara and pace bowler Curtly Ambrose return to form.
"The tourists appear doomed unless Brian Lara and Curtly Ambrose start to emerge from their respective form slumps and recapture their touch with bat and ball," Border wrote.
"Unless Ambrose is carrying an injury that is being shielded from public knowledge he needs a rocket."
Australia on Tuesday beat West Indies by 124 runs in the second test for a commanding 2-0 lead in the five-test series.
Lara and Ambrose are yet to make significant contributions on the Australian tour.

Lara, the world record holder for the highest score in test and first-class cricket, has scored just 73 runs in the first two tests at an average of 18.25, compared to his career average of just over 57.
Ambrose, the fourth highest wicket-taker in the history of West Indies test cricket, has taken three wickets in the two tests at a cost of 279 runs.

Border said he hoped the West Indies improved before the start of the third test in Melbourne on December 26. Australia need only a draw in Melbourne to retain the Frank Worrell Trophy they won last year.
"The Windies are forgeting the basics and they really need to sit down and have a team meeting and take a good hard look at where they're heading," Border said.
